Edibles in NYC

Edibles are the second-largest category on New York menus, with about 8,090 listings across the 69 licensed dispensaries we track, from 242 brands. The category runs from single 10-milligram drinks and two-pack tablets through gummies, chocolate, cookies and tinctures-in-disguise like shots, and it is where most of the city's lowest-priced products live. Ayrloom leads with 618 listings, followed by Camino at 595, Grön at 590, Wyld at 530, Off Hours at 455, 1906 at 274, MFNY at 257 and Eaton Botanicals at 251.

Prices start at $2.26, and 1906 drop pouches and Ayrloom single-serve drinks at $3 to $6 are the entry item at most shops. Standard 10-count gummy packs run $17 to $30 and 100-milligram chocolate bars about $25 before tax. Midtown has the deepest edible selection at about 1,120 listings, then Chelsea and Flatiron at 748, the Villages at 611, Sheepshead Bay at 461, Williamsburg at 442 and SoHo at 433, the only Manhattan neighborhood where edibles outnumber every other category. New York caps edibles at 10 milligrams of THC per serving and 100 milligrams per package, so a 20-count pack is 5 milligrams per piece.

Edibles FAQ
How long do edibles take to work?

Gummies and chocolate typically take 30 minutes to two hours, since THC is absorbed through digestion. Drinks from brands like Layup and Ayrloom use water-soluble THC and many people feel them in 15 to 30 minutes. Start with 5 milligrams or less if you are new.

What is the cheapest edible in New York City?

In our data, 1906 drop pouches are the floor, listed at $3 at Qube in Midtown and $3.10 to $3.50 at Purple Buds, Verdi Park Slope and Alta. Ayrloom and Layup single-serve drinks at $5 are the most common cheap item citywide.

Are cannabis drinks sold at every dispensary?

Nearly. Ayrloom is carried at 63 of the 67 shops we track, and most of them stock its single-serve 2:1 drinks. Layup, Tune, Weed Water, High Peaks, Harney Brothers and Cycling Frog are the other common drink brands.
